validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, not a GEM phantom. gem.wiki's own citation for this page is a single Youm7 (Al-Youm Al-Sabea) article dated 2021-01-21, 'Details of ongoing projects of the national natural gas network' (backlinks=8, i.e. it is the sole source cited for every field on the page). Fetched it directly: it lists a discrete project 'خط سفاجا / الغردقة بطول 38.5 كم – قطر24' (Safaga/Hurghada line, length 38.5 km, diameter 24 in), cost 362,000,000 EGP, planned completion January 2021 — an EXACT match to GEM's LengthKnown=38.50 km, Diameter=24 in, SegmentCost=362,000,000 EGP, StartYear1=2021. The article names the implementing company as الشركة المصرية للقازات الطبيعية (GASCO), one of the petroleum-sector companies, executing this line as part of the state's 'national natural gas network' reinforcement program. GulfPub (independent PE World Map database, Dec-2025 SDE scrape) carries a separate, structurally independent record 'Hurghada - Port Safaga Pipeline': operating, diameter 24 in (exact match), length 40 km (vs GEM's 38.5 km, ~4% delta — within normal rounding/route-definition variance), which corroborates existence, status, and diameter from a source with no textual overlap with the Youm7 report. NOT counted as a second independent narrative source: an almalnews.com article on the same GASCO 2021 reinforcement package repeats the identical 38.5 km/24 in/362M EGP/Jan-2021 figures verbatim — same government press packet, not independent corroboration (per SOP, republished wire copy doesn't count). So tier for the core specs is 'medium' (1 strong primary source + 1 independent Tier-2 database, not 2 fully independent narratives). DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against the full 51-row Egypt gas operating roster and the full GulfPub Egypt gas list — no other GEM row or GulfPub record plausibly describes this same physical pipe. It is distinct from GulfPub's separate 'Ras Shukheir - Hurghada' record (a different, northerly feeder segment, len 79 km) which supplies Hurghada from the north; P6034 is the next segment south, extending the grid from Hurghada to Safaga. No double-count identified. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission trunk — explicitly part of الشبكة القومية لللازات الطبيعية (national natural gas network), not a plant-internal or gathering line, not oil/NGL. FuelSource='Hurghada' (a place, not a field) is unusual phrasing but plausible here: this line is a downstream extension tapping the existing Hurghada city-gate supply (fed from the north by the Ras Shukheir-Hurghada trunk) rather than a wellhead-fed line — not flagged as an error.

validity.recommendation: Review Owner1: sheet lists 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS) at 100%, but EGAS does not own 100% of the entity that actually holds/operates Egypt's gas transmission grid. Per GASCO's own corporate record (English Wikipedia, sourced to GASCO/EGAS disclosures), GASCO — the company that operates the 22,000 km national gas transmission grid and, per the Youm7 source, physically built this specific line — is only ~70–79% owned by EGAS, with Petrojet and Egypt Gas Co. holding ~15% each. Likely fix: Owner1 should be 'Egyptian Natural Gas Company (GASCO)' (title-holder/operator of the asset), with EGAS noted as GASCO's majority (not sole) parent — or, if the sheet's convention is to record the ultimate state parent, the 100% figure should be corrected to reflect GASCO's actual EGAS/Petrojet/Egypt Gas Co. split. Worth checking whether this is a class-wide pattern across other Egypt GASCO-built trunk lines in the tracker (cf. the Owner=NIOC→NIGC/IGTC class fix already flagged for Iran).
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet's Owner [ref] cell is blank; current value Owner1='Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co', Owner1%=100.00%. The Youm7 source names the actual implementer/builder as الشركة المصرية للقازات الطبيعية (GASCO), described only as 'one of the petroleum-sector companies' — it does not state EGAS built or wholly owns this specific pipe. Independently, GASCO's English Wikipedia page (itself citing GASCO/EGAS corporate disclosures) states GASCO 'operates the gas grid with total length of 22,000 km' and that its main shareholder is EGAS at ~70–79% (infobox vs. body text disagree on the exact figure), with Petrojet and Egypt Gas Co. each holding ~15%. So EGAS at a flat 100% is very likely an oversimplification/error for this specific asset — I did NOT find any source stating EGAS itself (rather than GASCO) is title-holder of this pipe at 100%. Not fabricating a replacement Owner ref; flagging for human review rather than filling, per 'never auto-apply a reference value.'

routes.corridor_desc: Named endpoints are the cities of Hurghada and Safaga on Egypt's Red Sea coast, both in Red Sea Governorate, per the Youm7 government-report source and GulfPub's independent 'Hurghada - Port Safaga Pipeline' record. The two city centers are ~53 km apart by the coastal road (per general geography sources), while the sourced pipeline length is 38.5–40 km — shorter than the road distance, implying the true tie-in points are specific facilities (e.g. a compressor/city-gate station near southern Hurghada and a receiving point near northern Safaga) rather than the full city centers, and/or the line runs a more direct corridor than the coastal highway. No waypoint-level routing was found in any source; the plausible corridor is the narrow coastal strip between the two towns, generally paralleling the Red Sea coast road (Egypt route 32/Hurghada-Safaga road), but I could not source a specific alignment (inland vs. coastal, exact tie-in points) so I am not proposing intermediate waypoint coordinates.
routes.researcher_notes: City-level endpoint coordinates are well-established public geographic data (not fabricated), used only as approximate anchors since no facility-level tie-in point or route geometry could be sourced. Given the length mismatch vs. road distance between city centers, I'm keeping suggested_route_accuracy at 'low' rather than upgrading it — city-center coordinates alone do not defend a tighter corridor. A human routes-repo pass should look for GASCO grid maps or as-built drawings before drawing an actual line.

summary: P6034 (Hurghada–Safaga Gas Pipeline) is REAL and correctly classified: confirmed via an exact-match Youm7 government-report source (38.5km/24in/362M EGP/2021) plus independent GulfPub corroboration (dia=24 exact, len=40km ~4% delta) — verdict confirmed (caveat), tier medium (single narrative origin + 1 independent DB, not 2 independent narratives). One genuine attribution concern: Owner1='Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' at 100% is likely an oversimplification — GASCO (not EGAS) operates/likely titles the asset, and is only ~70-79% EGAS-owned (Petrojet/Egypt Gas Co. ~15% each) — flagged for human review, not auto-corrected. No duplicate or existence problem found. Route: named endpoints Hurghada/Safaga sourced with city-level coordinates; suggested_route_accuracy stays low pending a real corridor/tie-in-point source.
